title: Who Owns the Platform: What Black-Owned Sellers Pay Online | At The Margins, Ep. 6
lede: Shopify business owners are about twice as likely to be Black as comparable retail owners nationally (RAND). But on Amazon, a typical private-label seller pays an estimated 50–60% of sales back in fees (Marketplace Pulse). Episode 6 of At The Margins follows a sale online: Amazon's fees and the FTC's antitrust case, Etsy's fee structure, the platform programs for Black sellers and what happened to them, Canada's Black Entrepreneurship Program, and what the evidence says about platform design.
keyPoints: 15% of Shopify business owners are Black vs 7% of comparable retail and wholesale owners nationally (RAND, with Shopify, 2024).
On Shopify, Black owners' median platform revenue was $3,890 vs $13,528 for white owners; 36% vs 16% had a loan for their online business rejected (RAND, 2024).
A typical Amazon private-label seller paid an estimated 50–60% of sales in fees in 2023: ~15% referral, 20–35% fulfillment, up to 15% ads (Marketplace Pulse).
The FTC and 17 state AGs allege anti-discounting, Prime tied to Amazon fulfillment and fees near 50% of seller revenue; Amazon disputes it; trial set for March 29, 2027.
Shopify closed Build Black in January 2025; Amazon's $150M Black Business Accelerator hasn't published program-wide results we could find.
Yelp's Black-owned label raised weekly in-person visits about 10% (Aneja, Luca & Reshef, American Economic Review, 2025).
